ceiling_statement: For any feasible system under H1-H8, temporal and legal-state consistency can guarantee at most: (a) gapless monotone history - every admitted transition satisfies seq' = seq + 1 exactly, serialized through a single-writer admission point, so system history is a certificate-carrying total order with no gaps, repeats, or rollback (H4/H6); (b) append-only verifiability - any verifier holding any prior committed root verifies, by recomputing an RFC-6962 consistency proof, that the current log extends it; a verifier with no prior root can verify internal consistency only (wholesale replacement is undetectable to a fresh verifier - the fork-consistency bound, liftable only by an external witness quorum, a resource honestly absent today); (c) bitemporal legal-state soundness - the assertion 'legal state at valid-time t as known at transaction-time tau' is at most a pure, offline-replayable function (H5/H8) of the source snapshots and typed amendment events committed by tau under a declared formal amendment semantics, returning typed UNKNOWN (H2) for any (t, tau) not covered by committed evidence. No feasible system can assert legal state beyond its committed evidence, anticipate unpublished amendments, or exceed checkpoint-relative anti-rollback without real external witnesses.
derivation: (1) Evidence bound (information-theoretic): at transaction-time tau the system possesses exactly the bytes it has committed; an amendment the publisher has issued but the system has not captured is informationally absent, so the map (t, tau) -> state cannot exceed a function of the committed corpus at tau - and H1/H2 forbid statistical interpolation of the gap, forcing typed UNKNOWN. (2) Purity bound (verification theory): H5 + H8 require the (t, tau) view to be recomputable by a third party from committed inputs alone; any 'fresher' answer would depend on producer-declared, non-replayable state, violating H8 - so the deterministic bitemporal view over committed snapshots IS the ceiling, not an approximation of it. (3) Fork-consistency bound (Mazieres-Shasha): the transparency log alone proves internal append-only consistency; distinguishing the true history from a consistent fabricated one requires either a verifier-held prior root (prefix theorem via RFC-6962 consistency proofs) or a cosigning witness quorum - the latter is RESOURCE-dependent and B0 declares it disabled with no split-view-resistance claim (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp line 15), so consumer-floor-relative anti-rollback is the attainable maximum today. (4) Serialization bound (consistency/CAP-style): exactly-once gapless sequence increment requires a serialization point; a single-writer kernel (H4) attains it directly, and no coordination-free distributed scheme can guarantee it without consensus resources not declared here. In-force/implicit-repeal determinations are additionally interpretation-laden, which is why the legal-state half of the ceiling is only definable relative to a named formal amendment semantics.
relativity_note: Relative to a declared bitemporal amendment semantics: transaction-time = admission sequence of the Merkle-committed corpus (RFC-6962 leaf order); valid-time = publisher-declared in-force intervals; amendment effects = typed events (repeal, substitution, insertion) applied by an explicit event calculus in FRBR/Akoma-Ntoso-style versioning, as already used by the omega FRBR modules and the bitemporal records of source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp. Sub-bounds (a) and (b) - gapless monotone sequence and recompute-verified append-only consistency - are ABSOLUTE (model-independent); only the legal-state half (c) is semantics-relative, since 'in force at t' (vacatio legis, implicit repeal) has no model-free ground truth.
attainment_mechanism: All seats exist in-repo and compose with SBCL + ironclad crypto today. Keep: systems/orchestrator-epistemic/transparency-log.lisp (RFC-6962 consistency proofs, recomputed not trusted); systems/orchestrator-epistemic/artifact-census.lisp (prev_release_root chain); source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp (Ed25519 owner-pin, genTime-floor anti-rollback); source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp (bitemporal records + exact journal-prefix replay); JTMS amendment-impact in systems/orchestrator-cli/inference-gate.lisp. To attain the ceiling: (1) structural consumer floor - embed (tree root, sequence, Ed25519 signature) of the producing release in every emitted artifact, and make the verifier CLI fail closed (H3) unless a recomputed RFC-6962 consistency proof shows the current root extends the held floor, turning anti-rollback from 'consumer may supply a floor' into a refusal-by-default; (2) one total bitemporal seat - a single pure function View(t, tau) -> LegalState | UNKNOWN over Merkle-committed snapshots plus typed amendment events, returning typed UNKNOWN whenever committed coverage of (t, tau) fails (H2), replacing per-artifact consolidation; (3) serialize every admission through the single-writer kernel enforcing seq' = seq + 1 all-or-nothing (H6), executably enforced today via the OS-DAC single writer (authority-v2/capability/identities.sh + authority-v2/proofs/verify-capability-closure.sh) even before the formal kernel proof; (4) sign per-release checkpoints (Ed25519, present); witness cosigning remains spec-only, at-ceiling for declared resources.
b0_gap: Per the B0 map (AX-08 row): the tlog proves INTERNAL consistency only - wholesale replacement passes for a fresh verifier, and no structural consumer-floor embedding exists (anti-rollback currently needs a consumer-supplied floor); the kernel conjuncts :sequence-monotonic, :T3-no-rollback, :T5-monotonic-sequence are stated but 0 proved (authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp is spec-only - verified in-repo at lines 43-91); the external witness quorum is disabled with no split-view-resistance claim (authority-v2/log/witness-policy.sexp); bitemporal records exist (source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp, PRE-#4 FREEZE #4 current-record discipline) but there is no single total View(t, tau) seat over the whole corpus; genTime anti-rollback floors exist in the proof bundle but are not woven into every artifact.
lean_obligation: In Lean 4: (T5-monotone) model admission as a step relation K : State -> Input -> Option (State x Cert); prove forall s i s' c, K s i = some (s', c) -> s'.seq = s.seq + 1, and by induction every reachable trace from genesis has sequence list [0, 1, ..., n] with no gaps or repeats. (T3-prefix/anti-rollback) formalize RFC-6962 hashing (leafHash, nodeHash with domain separation) and prove, under a CollisionResistant SHA-256 hypothesis: verifyConsistency root_m root_n proof = true -> leaves_m <+: leaves_n; corollary: a verifier holding root_m detects any published root_n' whose log does not extend leaves_m. (Bitemporal soundness) for View : ValidTime -> TxTime -> Sum LegalState Unknown, prove (View t tau = inl s) -> DerivableFrom s (committedEvents tau) t (s follows from exactly the events with txTime <= tau whose validity covers t) and (not (Covered t tau)) -> View t tau = inr unknown (guessing structurally impossible, H2). (Tightness) exhibit two distinct well-formed logs with different content whose internal-consistency predicate both hold, showing a fresh verifier cannot separate them - the impossibility half establishing that (b) is the ceiling absent a witness quorum.
